subject: tech
title: What Is the Internet?
about: What the internet is: many computers joined to share information, Wi-Fi through the air and long cables under the ground and sea, websites, how a message or video is chopped into small numbered pieces and put back together like a puzzle, searching, checking facts with a grown-up, video calls, and what still works when the Wi-Fi is off. NC K2-NI-01 (information broken into pieces and reassembled), K2-CS-02 (what the router and Wi-Fi do) and K2-CS-04 (naming a slow or missing connection). Read it together: the tablet reads every question and choice aloud.
tip: Cut a drawing into four numbered pieces, carry them across the room one at a time, and put them back together: that is how a photo travels.

cards.note: The internet is many, many computers all over the world, joined up so they can share information.

cards.q: Computers on the internet are joined up. What do they share with each other?
cards.note: Pictures, messages, videos and games travel from computer to computer.

cards.q: Your tablet has no wires. How does the internet reach it?
cards.note: Wi-Fi sends invisible signals through the air, like a radio. A box at home called a router sends them out.

cards.q: How does the internet travel between faraway cities and across the ocean?
cards.note: Long cables run under the ground and along the bottom of the sea, joining countries together.

cards.q: What do we call a page you can visit on the internet?
cards.note: A website is a page of words, pictures and videos that lives on a computer somewhere, and you can look at it.

cards.q: You send Grandma a video. Does it travel in one big piece or in many small pieces?
cards.note: A computer chops the video into tiny pieces called packets. Small pieces travel faster and easier.

cards.q: The small pieces of a message arrive at Grandma's tablet. What happens next?
cards.note: Each piece has a number, like puzzle pieces, so the tablet knows how to put them in order.

cards.q: A photo is cut into pieces to travel. How does the other computer know the right order?
cards.note: Like numbered puzzle pieces: one, two, three. Put them in order and the picture is whole again.

cards.q: One piece of the video gets lost on the way. What does the tablet do?
cards.note: If a puzzle piece is missing, the tablet asks the other computer to send that piece again.

cards.q: You want to see pictures of real frogs. What helps you find them on the internet?
cards.note: Type what you want, and the search looks through millions of websites for you. Search with a grown-up.

cards.q: A website says dogs can fly. Is it true just because it is on the internet?
cards.note: Anyone can put things on the internet, even things that are wrong. A grown-up helps you check.

cards.q: Is the internet a person who talks to you, or lots of machines sharing information?
cards.note: When a game or video app talks, it is a program written by people, not a friend who knows you.

cards.q: Grandma lives far away. How can you see her face and talk to her today?
cards.note: A video call sends your picture and voice over the internet, chopped into pieces and put back together, fast.

cards.q: The Wi-Fi is off. Can you still draw in your drawing app?
cards.note: Drawing, saved games and photos live on the tablet, so they work without the internet.

cards.q: The tablet has no internet. Will a website open?
cards.note: Websites live on other computers, so they need the internet to reach you. A grown-up can turn the Wi-Fi back on.

cards.q: A video keeps stopping and spinning. What is probably the problem?
cards.note: The spinning circle means the pieces are arriving slowly. Saying the internet is slow helps a grown-up fix it.

cards.q: What is the box at home that sends the Wi-Fi out?
cards.note: The router is plugged into the wall and sends Wi-Fi through the house. If it is off, there is no internet.
